uncited: Topology and Ambiguity Handling resolves topological inconsistencies in standard lookup-table-based isosurface extraction when the isosurface passes through saddle points within a voxel [S1].

Standard lookup tables assign a fixed triangulation to ambiguous cases (e.g., 46, 47, 98, 99, 210, 213, 214, 215), which can cause cracks or holes if adjacent voxels resolve the ambiguity differently [S1].

Unlike [Lookup Table and Configuration](4978-lookup-table-and-configuration.md) which focuses on table generation, or [Marching Cubes Isosurface Tie-Breaking](10380-marching-cubes-isosurface-tie-breaking.md) which handles exact isovalue hits, this family enforces global manifold consistency through local patch or Hermite data constraints.
The family addresses the ambiguous case problem where the 8-bit sign pattern of a voxel's vertices does not uniquely determine the isosurface topology [S1].
In these configurations, the isosurface passes through the cube center, creating a saddle point [S1].
